BudgetWise is an ASP.NET Core Web API (.NET 8) and React/TypeScript/Vite/Tailwind personal-finance training app.

C#: PascalCase types/methods/properties; camelCase locals/parameters; descriptive names, focused methods, composition, C# 12 where appropriate, `var` when obvious, `using` inside namespaces, constructor DI and appropriate service lifetimes. Use consistent minimal APIs or controllers, RESTful plural-noun resources, correct HTTP methods/status codes, typed results, validation, DTOs (`record` for immutable DTOs), explicit mapping, camelCase JSON and Content-Type headers. Keep business logic in services; use built-in middleware.

Frontend: strict TypeScript, React hooks/functional components, focused reusable components, semantic accessible HTML/ARIA/keyboard navigation, Tailwind styling. Test user interactions with React Testing Library `screen`; mock APIs with MSW or similar.

Document public C# APIs with XML `<summary>`, `<param>`, `<returns>`, `<exception>` where applicable; explain why in comments. Add TypeScript JSDoc. Mark workshop TODOs `// TODO:` with clear descriptions and follow existing patterns. Prefer clarity, simple beginner-friendly code, and comments explaining .NET/React concepts.

Tests: xUnit, AAA, descriptive `MethodName_WhenCondition_ThenExpectedResult` names, `WebApplicationFactory<T>` integration tests, mocked external dependencies, success/failure/edge/boundary cases, accessibility tests. Test new features; update documentation. Check existing patterns, validate input, handle errors, generate tests, and ensure full-stack coherence.

Use in-memory collections for development/testing; populate realistic representative data via `MockData` in `Data/MockData.cs`; use thread-safe collections where needed. Initialize model properties; use navigation properties, nullable reference types appropriately, and `required` for mandatory properties.

Avoid inline styles; prefer Tailwind classes.
